answer: Neighborhood Cutoff Routing. Each agent advertises a routing neighborhood; peers accept only paths whose graph expansion stays within a verified local canyon of overlap. An agent must maintain distinct, mutually non-overlapping neighborhoods per identity, which forces sybils to build separate real connection subgraphs. Attacker cost: provisioning and sustaining N disjoint neighborhoods, each requiring organic traffic through a violet-tagged handshake, so cost scales linearly per identity. Isolated clusters get quarantined into a low-trust oasis.
